_comment: THE SUB-SESSION REGISTRY. One row per sub-session a manager has spawned.
WHY IT EXISTS, measured 2026-09-01: the two sub-sessions below existed ONLY
in the manager session's context. Had that session ended, nothing in the
repo named them -- no successor could have polled them, and both would have
been silently orphaned mid-work. This file is what makes a manager arriving
COLD able to resume rather than re-derive.
IT IS A REGISTRY, NOT A ROSTER OF THE REACHABLE -- BUT IT IS NOT TRUE THAT
A SUB-SESSION CANNOT BE REACHED. This block said 'A manager CANNOT message a
sub-session ... Verified by test, not assumed' until 2026-09-08. That test was
real and its conclusion was over-general: SendMessage and ListAgents do not
address a cloud session from a manager, and the note generalised from those two
mechanisms to the capability.
THE CHANNEL THAT WORKS: create_trigger with persistent_session_id set, then
fire_trigger on the returned id. Filed 2026-09-02 as
BL-20260902-AN-IDLE-CLOUD-SUB-SESSION-IS-RESUMABLE-VIA-A-SESSION-BOUND-ROUTINE-NOT-UNREACHABLE
and re-confirmed 2026-09-08 on two more sessions, which woke IDLE -> RUNNING and
acted on what they were poked with.
TWO LIMITS, both load-bearing. (1) IT IS ONE-WAY and the fired turn carries no
mcp__* tools. (2) IT IS NOT RELIABLE: of three sessions poked in one window on
2026-09-08, one did not resume -- fire_trigger returned SUCCESS while spawning a
FRESH session, and the only signal was that the returned session_id differed from
the persistent_session_id. So grade every poke with get_session on the TARGET id
before and after; never trust fire_trigger's own success.
A successor's moves are therefore: read this file, poll each id with get_session,
act on its branch/PR, POKE it when it is blocked on something only the manager
can answer, and archive it when its work has landed.
READ last_observed AS A SNAPSHOT, NEVER AS LIVE STATE. A sub-session's
needs_action is written at ITS last turn and cannot be cleared by the
manager handling the request. Phase C's still read 'open PR ... 403' long
after the PR was open. Poll get_session for current state; this file says
what EXISTS, not what is true right now.
